posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
I really hope this is just something strange with my own browser settings and it isn't affecting any other players, because that would be awful. Either way, I want to get to the bottom of this as fast as possible.
I was playing the Newgrounds upload of my game yesterday and saved. Today, when I hopped on to play it again, the save file was no longer there. I use the Brave web browser and have the setting on my browser to erase cached images and files on exit, however I just tested to see if it would erase the file if I exited Brave and it didn't. I can't for the life of me understand why it would randomly erase my file like that.
I am under the impression that RPG Maker MV web deployments save files into your browser's Local Storage, and I can confirm that I see the file right there in the developer menu under "Application > Local Storage >
https://uploads.ungrounded.com/
" so I'm unsure of what may have happened.
This is the first time I've ever uploaded a game to Newgrounds so I'm still pretty unsure of how it all works, but if anyone else has more knowledge on this it could be really helpful to me. Thank you. I'll continue to do more testing as well.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
I remember seeing this happen on GameJolt or Itch.io; if I find the thread I'll post it here, but it was something related to cross-origin, meaning the game was inside an IFRAME on a subdomain:
www .examplehosting . com
--> gamehtml5 .examplehosting . com
So it's possible that when opening the game directly from the iframe URL, the save files are loaded into the list normally.
This would be related to Google Chrome's native tracker blocker:
Turn "Do Not Track" on or off - Computer - Google Chrome Help
When you browse the web on computers or Android devices, you can send a request to websites not to collect or track your browsing data. It's turned off by default. However, what happens to your
support.google.com
EDIT:
I performed some tests and, even after removing the permission block, saved games disappeared from all games created with RMMV that use local storage and from RMMZ that uses IndexedDB.
The block doesn't appear if you log in through the main domain, as it's linked to the subdomain.
Then, I accessed the settings:
Privacy and Security > Cookies > Browsing data > "Always clear cookies when closing windows".
And I obtained the following result:
I removed it, saved the game, closed the browser and reopened it, and the last save was still there.

I'm not sure I completely understand what is going on here to be honest lol.
At least in Brave, there is an option to clear cookies and other site data when you close a website. I have that option turned off both globally and for Newgrounds.
Now, it does have this window:
The burger menu on Ungrounded lets me select the option to "Allow to set third-party cookies." Could the browser potentially be thinking that, since it is an iframe from a "third party," it is not saving any of the data? I do have the global setting to block third-party cookies turned on, but that's also a default in any Brave installation and I'm not having issues in other installations.
It does seem like clicking the option to "Allow to set third-party cookies" does
NOT
, in fact, maintain the save data.
It looks like, on all my other Brave installations (including that other account) that option was never even there. So Ungrounded was allowed to set third-party cookies by default, despite the default option for a Brave install being to block third-party cookies. Either way, it seems like it doesn't change anything.
It also seems like Incognito is not what is erasing the file. It seems to be simply... time? I'm not sure exactly. I can save the game, close the tab and re-open and it'll still be there, but close it and give it a few minutes and it's gone the next time. Maybe something is like... corrupted with wherever my local storage is? Again, sorry to keep saying this but it ONLY happens on this one Brave profile. Not on my newly created profile, not on my other computers running Brave, not on Firefox or Edge.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Another test you can do is save the game and close only the tab, without closing the browser, then reopen the game page and see if the save is still there.
If it works, then the data is indeed deleted when you close the browser. Go to the search bar in settings and type "clear" or paste this address:
brave://settings/?seach=clear
I found several settings related to this.
